## Goal

Continue the trained YAT embedding-v1 checkpoint (step 14,000) to improve multilingual, semantic and code representations while preserving earlier capabilities and model lineage. This audit created 22 evidence-backed work items. No P0 corruption or defect in the existing public weights was established. Static review and metadata reproductions do not qualify changed training on TPUs.

## Before substantial continuation

1. Correct known-positive negative masking, authenticate parent and resume identities, and validate prepared data (#39–#46).
2. Integrate held-out representation/regression gates and replayable multilingual data selection (#47–#48).
3. Freeze runtime/source setup and qualify the hard-negative path and recovery on physical TPU (#50, #52).
4. Strengthen complete evaluation receipts (#57–#59). Profile and scale only after the quality candidate passes (#49).
5. Validate the exact exported release and expanded parity before new publication (#53, #60).

The legacy cleanup issue #51 applies when that old launcher is used; prefer the existing guarded supervisor. Operational refactoring, actual billing and storage accounting are #54–#56. Expensive GitHub checks remain paused under the user's existing preference.

## Audit work items

- [ ] #39 — Exclude all known relevant documents from the mined-negative denominator (TRAIN-01)
- [ ] #40 — Authenticate parent checkpoint semantics before a fresh embedding stage (TRAIN-02)
- [ ] #41 — Include sampler, imported kernels, and numerical runtime in exact-resume identity (TRAIN-03)
- [ ] #42 — Validate prepared embedding token schemas and padding against the encoder (TRAIN-04)
- [ ] #43 — Reject resume cursors beyond stop-after and emit explicit completion status (TRAIN-05)
- [ ] #44 — Unify cross-source duplicate identity and train/dev quarantine (TRAIN-06)
- [ ] #45 — Use code-aware text identity instead of casefolding code (TRAIN-07)
- [ ] #46 — Make tokenizer truncation policy explicit in embedding preparation (TRAIN-08)
- [ ] #47 — Gate embedding continuation on representation quality and preserve best checkpoints (TRAIN-09)
- [ ] #48 — Generalize replayable dataset/language sampling for representation continuation (TRAIN-10)
- [ ] #49 — Qualify embedding scaling and remove avoidable encoding and input overhead (TRAIN-11)
- [ ] #50 — Add direct physical-TPU coverage for hard-negative embedding training and recovery (TRAIN-12)
- [ ] #51 — Unify GCP launch paths behind an independently verified cloud lease (INFRA-01)
- [ ] #52 — Lock embedding training/evaluation environments and source overlays (INFRA-02)
- [ ] #53 — Bind PyTorch parity to published artifacts and reject nonfinite gate values (INFRA-03)
- [ ] #54 — Replace device-based cost guesses with verified slice rates and billing reconciliation (INFRA-04)
- [ ] #55 — Use manifest-driven launches and bounded telemetry uploads (INFRA-05)
- [ ] #56 — Track retained storage and cleanup plans across training stages (INFRA-06)
- [ ] #57 — Require finite scores and exact split/subset coverage for complete evaluations (EVAL-001)
- [ ] #58 — Bind evaluation receipts to source, runtime and aggregation protocol (EVAL-002)
- [ ] #59 — Route embedding evaluator and PyTorch changes to appropriate validation (EVAL-003)
- [ ] #60 — Expand physical-TPU conversion parity beyond eight 128-token inputs (EVAL-004)

## Existing open work retained

- #1 — repository-wide quality umbrella.
- #12 — generic physical multi-host acceptance; new embedding-specific coverage is #50.
- #11 — patch release readiness.
- #19 — public checkpoint/demo release contract.
- #23 — decoder cross-harness baseline protocol; not an EmbeddingGemma comparison.
- #31 — Kaggle-specific prepared input path; outside this GCP continuation's priority.

## Documentation and tools

Local versioned audit dossier: docs/SYSTEM_AUDIT_2026-09-30.md and docs/audit-2026-09-30/. Canonical runbook: docs/REPRESENTATION_TRAINING_RUNBOOK.md. Tool inventory: docs/TRAINING_TOOLS.md. Reusable skill: skills/flaxchat-training/SKILL.md. These documentation edits are local working-tree changes until separately committed/published.

Use existing JAX/NNX/Optax, Orbax, prepared data, GCP cleanup guards and MTEB infrastructure. Add the missing integrations rather than a new framework. XProf and available Billing export support measurement; no paid tool platform is required.

## Completion gate

- [ ] Relevant correctness, data and identity issues resolved with reproducible evidence.
- [ ] Physical TPU loss/gradient/recovery qualification on the chosen topology passes.
- [ ] Declared held-out representation gates improve while preserving required language/code capabilities.
- [ ] Cost cap, last-good checkpoint and independent cleanup owner are recorded.
- [ ] Final benchmark and publication claims remain bound to immutable model/protocol artifacts.

Audited working tree based on d64a0d18cac0343a936c13ebea6ce02be5adf879, including uncommitted embedding code. No cloud allocation, model execution, workflow activation or bucket deletion was performed by this audit.

## October 1 reconciled audit — three parallel reviewers

Reviewed the current dirty working tree based on d64a0d18cac0343a936c13ebea6ce02be5adf879. All 29 open issues were refreshed. The 22 original audit findings already have issues; the remaining observations below extend those issues, rather than creating duplicates or closing unqualified work. No historical corruption of the public weights is established.

### Five remaining P1 code defects

- #47 / #50: Failed development gates save a recovery cursor without the last evaluation/failure decision. Resume checks baseline against itself and can continue from the failed model. Persist authenticated failed status and test intermediate/horizon failure across repeated resume before any optimizer update or successful completion.
- #42: Shared data admission hashes only manifest-listed entries, while loading every required array. Require complete canonical train/dev checksum inventory; missing entries and same-shaped in-range mutations must fail admission.
- #39 / #42: Raw negative presence is not checked against loaded negative_valid flags. Derive or compare row flags and reject pair/triplet disagreement before allocation.
- #40 / #42 / #52: Optional parent-checkpoint preflight creates a writable cleanup-enabled Orbax manager. Use a nonmutating committed-metadata reader with corrupt/missing/uncommitted/concurrent-artifact tests and no backend initialization.
- #53 / #58 / #60: Parity computes complete provenance but stores only packages/source hashes. Retain interpreter, numerical settings, effective configuration and deployment identity; reject changed identity across cases before publication.

### Remaining P2 implementation work

- #47: recall_at_k currently measures first-relevant hit rate for multi-positive queries; correct naming/denominator and version the metric policy.
- #52 / #55: Historical MIRACL and upload wrappers still use floating installs/source paths; replace them with equivalent hashed manifest recipes.
- #54: Provisioning does not attach the run labels expected by billing attribution; verify supported labels and reconcile real posted resource identities.
- #55: Signal after child exit during final upload can prevent the status receipt; persist original return code before telemetry and test the signal window.
- #60: Full parity test remains monolithic despite a bounded per-case worker; schedule and resume missing immutable cases independently.
- #53 / #60: Generic parity still assumes layer 10 exists; derive indices or reject unsupported depths before allocation.
- #54: Budget reservations coordinate one shared filesystem only. Use one campaign owner; add cloud reservations only if independent controllers are introduced.

### Implemented fixes and evidence limits

Shared stage policy admission, stage-global evaluation cadence, best/recent commit reconciliation, optimizer-counter checks, actual training output-path binding, live package/interpreter inventory checks, bounded capacity waits, immutable task inventories, finite scores, zero-vector parity guards and generic export stage identity are implemented locally. Do not reopen the earlier descriptions as absent fixes. They are not merged or physically accepted by their presence.

Local model-free verification: **92 metadata tests, 9 subtests, and 10 standalone stage/contract tests passed**. **78 Markdown files passed validation**; repository and installed training skills passed schema validation, with an independent forward review. No CPU model work, new TPU qualification, workflow dispatch, cloud allocation or storage deletion ran during this audit.

The embedding-specific physical multi-host worker now defines ownership, global loss/full-parameter-gradient references and four-update GCS resume checks. It has not run on physical multi-host hardware; sustained training, abrupt worker/transport loss, v6e and all-scale acceptance remain unproven.

Actual pinned retrieval/bitext/STS/code development data, programming-language coverage, large-mixture host-memory measurement, representative real MTEB split/subset receipt acceptance, matched mmBERT/EmbeddingGemma runs, and CodeSearchNet/CoIR overlap audit remain product/evidence work. Historical scores and paper columns stay separately labeled.

### Concrete next gate

Fix the four P1 training admission/recovery defects; freeze source/runtime/parent/data identities; run one bounded physical single-host objective/cache/recovery qualification; then qualify the intended multi-host topology and profile scale before substantial continuation. Release parity defects apply before publication and do not block a training-only correctness run. Continue existing trained YAT weights with bias 1, epsilon 0.01 and trainable alpha.

Updated local artifacts: docs/SYSTEM_AUDIT_2026-10-01.md, docs/ISSUE_READINESS_CHECKLIST.md, docs/TRAINING_TOOLS.md, docs/REPRESENTATION_TRAINING_RUNBOOK.md, skills/flaxchat-training/SKILL.md and independent review/source-validation receipts under docs/audit-2026-09-30/. These changes remain local until committed/pushed.

## October 1 implementation reconciliation

Three parallel agents completed training/data, infrastructure, and evaluation/release review and fixes. This supersedes the earlier comment’s “remaining code defects” status; original findings remain historical evidence. All 29 issues stay open until their actual acceptance criteria pass.

Implemented locally: complete canonical array checksums and raw negative-valid agreement (#39/#42); authenticated failed-development-gate persistence with v2 policy and fractional recall (#47/#50); nonmutating stdlib-only committed-checkpoint reader (#40/#42/#52); signal-safe terminal status, reviewed frozen wrapper routes and normalized provider labels/read-back enforcement (#52/#54/#55); full v3 backend parity identity, depth-aware intermediates and bounded missing-case campaigns (#53/#58/#60).

Final selected model-free verification: **124 tests and 48 subtests passed**. No CPU model execution or new physical TPU qualification. MTEB 2.21.8 metadata checks are not emitted benchmark results. The retained step-14,000 checkpoint’s committed JSON evidence passed the read-only reader; this does not verify tensor restoration. Changes remain local, unmerged and physically unqualified. Expensive GitHub workflows remain undispatched.

Next gates in order:
1. Complete/freeze the embedding runtime: the older generic validation lock lacks Safetensors required by export/trainer fixtures.
2. Run bounded physical single-host objective/cache/full-gradient/optimizer/recovery tests, including failed-gate restarts.
3. Prepare actual pinned multilingual retrieval/bitext/STS/code development data, baseline the retained parent, preserve programming-language provenance and audit code benchmark overlap.
4. Qualify sustained physical multi-host recovery/abrupt loss, then warmed profiling and intended scale/device families. v6e/all scales remain unvalidated.
5. Execute expanded physical parity and actual MTEB receipt/merge/resume coverage; matched mmBERT/EmbeddingGemma comparisons and immutable new-release verification remain pending.
6. Reconcile actual posted billing and explicit retained-storage policy.

Updated local delivery: docs/SYSTEM_AUDIT_2026-10-01.md, docs/ISSUE_READINESS_CHECKLIST.md, docs/TRAINING_TOOLS.md, docs/REPRESENTATION_TRAINING_RUNBOOK.md and skills/flaxchat-training/SKILL.md; the installed skill is synchronized. Continue existing YAT weights with fixed bias 1, epsilon 0.01 and trainable alpha.

## October 1 physical follow-up and parallel tool upgrades

The corrected frozen embedding runtime installed offline on physical TPU v5 lite (8 devices, one host; Python 3.12.14, JAX/JAXlib 0.11.1, Flax 0.12.9, Optax 0.2.8). Required imports and provider run/stage label read-back passed. The first attempt failed before model execution on an optional interpreter terminal-database link; the derived headless artifact preserves all retained runtime files and keeps extraction safety checks. Both attempts’ owned TPU VMs and queued resources are independently verified NOT_FOUND. Storage was preserved.

**Physical acceptance: 14 passed, 2 failed, zero skipped.** All four hard-negative objective/gradient cases and all nine trainer cases passed, including off-cadence stops, best-checkpoint reconciliation, intermediate/horizon failed-quality-gate restarts and rejected-update state retention. The global cache/RNG reference passed. Both NNX YAT cache cases failed at optimizer-state leaf comparisons; their earlier loss, gradient and updated-model assertions passed. Tolerances remain unchanged. Added named-leaf numerical diagnostics for the next physical run; BF16 shape-dependent roundoff is a hypothesis, not a proved diagnosis. No unchanged automatic retry or third allocation was launched.

Three parallel agents added programming-language provenance/exposure reporting, a bounded SQLite exact-overlap auditor, a pinned development-only recipe/exporter, and isolated peer-loss/local-SSH-attachment-loss campaigns. Metadata fixtures do not qualify physical faults; local attachment loss does not mean whole-controller SIGKILL or real network outage. Actual data preparation, parent exposure and cross-source quarantine remain required before tuning.

**Selected model-free checks: 150 passed, 55 subtests passed.** 85 Markdown files validated. No CPU model forward/backward/benchmark ran; expensive GitHub workflows remain undispatched. The training skill is upgraded and synchronized.

Local raw TPU/JUnit evidence: docs/audit-2026-09-30/physical-qualification-02/. Follow-up: docs/audit-2026-09-30/physical-qualification-2026-10-01.md. Source archive SHA-256: bd4e7d7684c5767fab44a59e89d920e3fba2321c1805ef46055b10231005d25e. Changes remain local/unmerged.

All 29 issues stay open pending their complete acceptance criteria. Next gate: identify the cache optimizer leaf before changing numerics; then qualify actual pinned development data and retained production-parent restoration. Sustained multi-host recovery, v6e/scales, production quality, matched competitor measurements and expanded release parity remain open.

## Problem

The three plans in `benchmarks/baselines/` remain `pending_matched_run`. Current README comparisons describe framework features but do not provide controlled flaxchat, nanochat, and MaxText measurements under the canonical protocol.

## Proposal

Implement adapters and execute all three trainers on the same single-accelerator hardware with identical tokenized batches and controlled model size.

## Acceptance criteria

- All three source repositories and dataset inputs use immutable revisions.
- Actual trainable parameter counts fall within the protocol tolerance.
- Tokenized batches, optimizer semantics, precision, warmup, and measured steps match.
- Records include compile time, steady tokens/sec, MFU, peak memory, checkpoint latency, validation quality, and limitations.
- `python -m benchmarks.compare --protocol benchmarks/protocol.yaml ...` passes.
- Raw logs and records are archived; negative results are retained.
- Documentation makes no apples-to-apples claim until every record passes validation.

comments.body:
Implementation and evidence update from PR #25:

- Immutable comparison adapters now run flaxchat, nanochat, and MaxText sequentially in one Kaggle P100 kernel over the same generated/tokenized batches.
- CPU preflight v4 passed at flaxchat `08f21ea3c5d4455560ba56c349af8f7a2c42c8b9`, nanochat `a445144d3905c6845fda2d3cab8e63248a70cd32`, and MaxText `87b18614b0ef6c68c4be43b4396c695645ecf055`.
- Counts were 589,902 / 589,902 / 606,848 against the 600,000 ±5% gate. The strengthened preflight also completed a native nanochat forward/backward AdamW update with GPU and TPU disabled.
- P100 v2 retained a negative result for a PyTorch wheel that omitted `sm_60`; P100 v3 proved the pinned `torch==2.5.1+cu118` runtime supports `sm_60`, then retained a second negative result exposing int32 targets at PyTorch cross-entropy. Flaxchat and MaxText completed in both bundles.
- The adapter now promotes token IDs and targets to `torch.int64`, with focused tests and the CPU-native optimizer-step gate passing.

No apples-to-apples performance claim has been published because all three records have not yet passed in one bundle. After two GPU attempts, another P100 run is intentionally held for an explicit quota decision rather than consuming accelerator quota automatically.

issues.body:
## Problem

Kaggle version 6 validates eight TPU devices on one host. Synthetic virtual-device and cross-topology checkpoint tests do not prove multi-process coordination, host-local data partitioning, collective behavior, or recovery on physical TPU workers.

## Proposal

Run a bounded multi-host Cloud TPU acceptance job using the documented immutable environment and archive machine-readable evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- At least two physical processes initialize before any JAX backend query.
- The manifest records source SHA, image/environment digest, topology, slice/process/device counts, zone, and commands.
- Host batches are disjoint and together reproduce the global order.
- A synchronized training step produces finite matching losses and expected shardings.
- Checkpoints restore across multi-host to single-host and single-host to multi-host topology.
- One interrupted/preempted run resumes without repeating or skipping a batch.
- Logs and a structured summary are committed or attached with cost and limitations.

comments.body:
PR #25 now makes the eventual paid physical multi-host acceptance fail fast and auditable before longer phases:

- `infra/tpu/flexstart.sh` defaults to a one-hour `v5litepod-16` request and refuses `create` before any `gcloud` call unless `FLAXCHAT_APPROVE_PAID_RUN=I_UNDERSTAND_TPU_BILLING` is explicitly set.
- `scripts.multihost_acceptance run` imports the distributed initializer before backend discovery, requires at least two physical processes and a TPU backend, records exact source/environment/location/topology metadata, proves disjoint host-local batches reconstruct canonical global order, creates a `PartitionSpec('data', None)` global array, and executes one synchronized finite gradient update.
- Every worker emits a structured record. The offline `summarize` command fails closed on missing/duplicate processes, overlapping/duplicate batches, digest drift, revision/environment/topology disagreement, non-finite or mismatched loss, and missing worker success. It requires actual billed cost and states that checkpoint/resume phases remain unproven.
- The real JAX path passed locally on four synthetic CPU devices with four addressable data shards; 27 focused tests, Ruff, Pyright, shell syntax, and docs checks passed. GitHub Linux validation passed at `0007b13` in 4m11s. No Cloud TPU was provisioned.

Issue #12 remains open: physical multi-host probe evidence, multi-host↔single-host checkpoint restore, and an interrupted physical resume still require explicit paid-infrastructure authorization. The new probe is intended to prevent spending on those longer phases if the slice is unexpectedly single-host or worker coordination is unhealthy.

## Objective

Prove flaxchat as a reproducible, end-to-end JAX/Flax LLM training system on CPU/GPU and Cloud TPU.

## Required work

- [ ] Make the TinyStories tokenizer→pretrain→SFT→RL→evaluation→inference path reproducible from a clean checkout.
- [ ] Add CPU smoke tests so core correctness is testable without accelerator access.
- [ ] Add GPU and TPU CI/periodic runs for training, checkpointing, restore, sharding, and generation.
- [ ] Publish loss curves, throughput, memory, compile time, and scaling efficiency with exact hardware/configuration.
- [ ] Compare equivalent configurations against nanochat and a relevant JAX baseline such as MaxText.
- [ ] Test single-host and multi-host checkpoint portability and interrupted-training recovery.
- [ ] Validate speculative decoding output correctness and measure accepted-token speedup.
- [ ] Pin datasets, tokenizer inputs, evaluation versions, and random seeds; document provenance and licensing.
- [ ] Add configuration schemas, failure messages, architecture diagrams, and operator documentation.
- [ ] Publish a small checkpoint and an automated inference demonstration when licensing permits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clean CPU smoke tests pass on every PR and accelerator runs publish artifacts periodically.
- [ ] At least one full small-model training run is independently reproducible.
- [ ] Benchmark results include scripts, configurations, logs, and limitations.
- [ ] Tagged releases preserve checkpoint and configuration compatibility.

## Path-specific implementation map

### Training engine and distributed execution

- [ ] In `flaxchat/config.py`, replace loose configuration with validated dataclasses/schema covering model, tokenizer, data, optimizer, mesh, precision, checkpoint, evaluation, and generation; serialize the resolved config into every run.
- [ ] In `flaxchat/engine.py` and `execution.py`, separate pure train/eval steps from orchestration, compilation, device mesh setup, logging, and failure recovery.
- [ ] Add single-device and synthetic multi-device tests for parameter sharding, optimizer-state sharding, gradient accumulation, loss scaling, donation, and deterministic RNG folding.
- [ ] In `flaxchat/checkpoint.py`, add atomic temporary writes, manifest hashes, version metadata, async completion, partial-checkpoint detection, resharding, and interrupted-save recovery tests.
- [ ] In `dataloader.py`, `dataset.py`, and `prefetch.py`, version dataset manifests and test shard ordering, host partitioning, resume offsets, packing boundaries, corrupted examples, and backpressure.
- [ ] In `flaxchat/gpt.py`, add tiny configurations testing attention masks, RoPE positions, KV caches, tied embeddings, precision, scanning/rematerialization, and reference parity.

### End-to-end reproducibility and evaluation

- [ ] Make `scripts/run_tinystories.py` the canonical small E2E runner that emits a run manifest, tokenizer hash, data hash, resolved config, logs, checkpoint, eval metrics, and sample output.
- [ ] Refactor `scripts/pretrain.py`, `sft.py`, `rl.py`, and `eval.py` into thin CLI wrappers over reusable functions under `flaxchat/`; test the functions directly.
- [ ] In `flaxchat/eval.py`, pin task versions and add aggregation confidence intervals, sample counts, prompt templates, generation parameters, and raw prediction export.
- [ ] Add `benchmarks/` with comparable nanochat/MaxText configs and a parser that reports tokens/sec, model FLOPs utilization, compile time, memory, checkpoint time, and scaling efficiency.
- [ ] In `scripts/chat_cli.py` and `chat_web.py`, share one generation service and test streaming cancellation, sampling determinism, context limits, and checkpoint/tokenizer mismatch.

### Local, cloud, and release paths

- [ ] Keep `scripts/train_local.py`, `train_tpu.py`, and `train_kaggle.py` as adapters around the same engine/config; avoid platform-specific training logic forks.
- [ ] Add `infra/tpu/` with a documented launcher, immutable environment/image reference, worker coordination, log collection, shutdown, and cost guardrails.
- [ ] Add CPU PR tests in `.github/workflows/`, scheduled accelerator benchmarks, coverage, type/lint checks, dependency auditing, package builds, and artifact retention.
- [ ] Add `docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md`, `docs/SHARDING.md`, `docs/CHECKPOINT_FORMAT.md`, and `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` linked to executable commands.
- [ ] Move or clearly label `torch_port/` as a validation baseline; add parity tests and ensure it is not counted as an independent implementation.
